newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank sees single-digit loan growth.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank sees single-digit loan growth.

text.p: NationsBank Corp. investor relations executive Susan Carr said on Tueday that loan growth would hover in the high single digits for the 1996 fourth quarter.
Carr said at the end of September loan growth had picked up in the commerical and consumer sectors, particularly for mortgages and credit cards.
"Based on what we saw at the end of the third quarter and the first part of October, I would say that we hope for something in the seven percent to nine percent type range," Carr said.
Carr made the comments during a conference call with reporters after NationsBank posted record earnings of $625 million, or $2.12 per share, earlier Tuesday.
Analysts had expected the bank to earn $2.05 per share in the quarter, according to I/B/E/S. The results compared with $530 million, or $1.95, in the same period a year ago.

Carr said the strong earnings were the result of steady revenue growth and expense management. The bank's efficiency ratio improved to 55.9 percent, down from 56.7. "It's good net interest income growth with even stronger fee income growth, good expense control and pretty stable credit costs...."

Carr also said NationsBank benefitted from its stock repurchase program announced in July. She said 13.3 million shares were repurchased in the third quarter, or $1.2 billion worth of stock. That compares with a stock buyback plan of 9.8 million shares in all of 1995.
"Share repurchases will continue to be a part of our capital management program," Carr said.

NationsBank previously announced its $9.46 billion acquisition of St. Louis-based Boatmen's Bancshares would impact projections for double-digit earnings per share growth next year. The deal is due to close in January.

Projections were for NationsBank' earnings per share growth to range between 12 percent and 15 percent this year. Carr said that level would not be sustained throughout 1997, however, because of the Boatmen's acquisition.

But double-digit earnings per share growth should be restored by 1998, she added. "We've (previously) announced to the investment community that we do think there will be about 5 to 6 percent earnings dilution from the Boatmen's transaction which we will then expect to eliminate by the end of next year so that in 1998 you start picking up again the double-digit earnings per share growth."
